title: 5. Narrative Device Tropes
use_cases: Use when structuring a novel through non-traditional communication like letters or text messages
Implement when creating a contrast between a character's internal written thoughts and their external reality
Configure when balancing perspective between a living protagonist and a supernatural or deceased narrator
Use when researching examples of polyvocal storytelling and genre-specific narrative devices
content:
- Letters/Texts Only – Epistolary dual POV (e.g., This Is How You Lose the Time War by Amal El-Mohtar & Max Gladstone).
- Diary vs. Reality – One POV is written, one is lived (e.g., The Silent Patient by Alex Michaelides).
- Afterlife/Present Life – One POV is dead or otherwise supernatural (e.g., The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue by V.E. Schwab, A Certain Slant of Light by Laura Whitcomb).

Okay! Hope that was helpful to you. See also David Long’s list of “Polyvocal” stories for some more examples of dual POV.
